newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO in war of words ahead of U.S. mission.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO in war of words ahead of U.S. mission.

text.p: Israel and the Palestinians traded accusations on Thursday ahead of a U.S. mission to salvage Middle East peacemaking battered by a twin suicide bombing and Jewish settlement of occupied Arab land.
Yasser Arafat lashed out in a newspaper interview against measures imposed by Israel on Palestinians since two Islamic suicide bombers killed 13 people last week at an Israeli market.

"(Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu has declared war on us and we have to prepare for what will come. The situation is serious," the Palestinian president said in an interview published in Israel's daily Yedioth Ahronoth.

Responding to Arafat's reported remarks, Netanyahu said in a speech to members of his Likud party: "I want to warn against any attempt by the Palestinian Authority to create so-called spontaneous violence."
Netanyahu called on the self-rule administration to wage "a bitter war" against the infrastructure of the militant Moslem groups Hamas and Islamic Jihad and "end the climate of violence".

The foreign ministers of Egypt and Jordan, meeting in Alexandria, said it was dangerous to leave the latest peace crisis unresolved and repeated their concerns at Israel's sanctions against the Palestinians.
Arafat's own Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) faction Fatah told a Gaza news conference on Thursday it was "ready for all options".

After the market attack, Israel halted peace talks with the PLO and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza, stopping trade and keeping thousands of Palestinians from jobs in Israel. Israel's Treasury froze transfer of tax duties it owes the Palestinians.
Israel has also rounded up scores of suspected Moslem militants and threatened to re-enter Palestinian-ruled areas if Arafat failed to crack down on them in territory he controls.

Arafat told reporters in Gaza regarding the sanctions: "Are the Palestinian people field experiments for Israeli punishments to be run on them from time to time? Aren't they human beings and shouldn't they be treated in a humane way?"

Despite the war of words, all sides welcomed U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright's saying she might at month's end visit the region. U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross is due as early as Saturday night.

"There was a call between her and me yesterday and I thanked her for her speech which she made yesterday that showed the care of the U.S. to push the peace process and save it from the current crisis," Arafat said in Gaza.
"We will welcome her and anyone else who can help restore security," Netanyahu said.
Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, his Jordanian colleague Fayez al-Tarawnah and the Arab League also welcomed the possible visit as a positive step.
"The danger of the present situation is its continuation. Egypt and Jordan are coordinating on how to salvage the peace process," Moussa said.

Albright, in a speech on Wednesday, said her trip depended on an improved security situation. President Bill Clinton warned the peace process could not go on unless the Palestinians halted "terrorist" acts like the Jerusalem bombing.
Albright and Clinton also criticised Israel for taking unilateral steps, including building Jewish settlements on occupied Arab land, that enraged the Palestinians.
Netanyahu says the punitive measures taken since the bombing will remain in force and the peace talks will stay in limbo until Arafat fights militants.

Arafat says he has fought militants despite cutting security cooperation with Israel in March when Netanyahu broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. He says settlement of areas Israel occupied in 1967 pre-empts final peace talks.
Also on Thursday, Palestinian sources said Israeli authorities demolished four Arab homes in the West Bank built without a licence. The army said it was checking the report.
In south Lebanon, pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas killed a pro-Israeli Lebanese militiaman in a car-bomb attack. Israeli shelling then killed one Lebanese civilian and wounded two.
Later a roadside bomb exploded in south Lebanon beside a car travelling in Israel's occupation zone, killing a mother and her two children and wounding a man, Israeli military sources said.
